rounds.note: A short call before the interviews.

rounds.name: Machine coding
rounds.note: A UI build: plain JavaScript in the 2020–2021 prompts that name a stack, mostly React in 2024–2025 accounts.

rounds.name: JavaScript and React concepts
rounds.note: Questions and short coding tasks on JavaScript and React: output prediction, polyfills and promises.

rounds.name: Algorithms and problem solving
rounds.note: Data-structure and algorithm problems, usually one or two per round.

rounds.name: Design
rounds.note: Low-level class design in two Bangalore loops from 2020 and 2021, application or component design in 2024.

rounds.name: Behavioural and hiring manager
rounds.note: A hiring manager round, technical in a 2020 and a 2021 Bangalore loop.

rounds.name: As Appropriate round
rounds.note: A final one-hour round with an interviewer at GM or Partner level, in a 2020 Bangalore loop.

rounds.name: Initial interview
rounds.note: An initial interview, held virtually like every student interview.

rounds.name: Final interview
rounds.note: A second and final interview for students selected after the first, also virtual.

rounds.name: Recruiter conversation
rounds.note: A long conversation in the 2020 account.

rounds.name: Hiring-manager conversation
rounds.note: A long behavioural interview with a UI manager in the 2020 account; a 2024 commenter expects a manager screen.

rounds.name: Technical screen
rounds.note: One hour with three small JavaScript tasks in a 2025 screen for an L4 or L5 frontend role.

rounds.name: Take-home
rounds.note: A UI built at home, in two 2020 accounts, one of which reviewed it in the onsite.

rounds.name: Onsite
rounds.note: One coding interview, a take-home review and two behavioural interviews in 2020, with no LeetCode-type questions.

variants.title: New graduates and interns
variants.ask: Interviewing as a new graduate or intern?

rounds.name: Take-home assessment
rounds.note: A take-home assessment opens the process.

rounds.name: Interview rounds
rounds.note: Two rounds for new graduates and about two to three for interns, advancing on the feedback at each stage.

rounds.name: Résumé review
rounds.note: About one week before the recruiting team emails back, per the interview guide.

rounds.name: Recruiter or hiring-manager call
rounds.note: A conversation with the hiring manager or recruiter about work experience, motivations and goals.

rounds.name: Technical screen
rounds.note: Coding, then system design, back to back in a 2024 senior frontend screen, neither run by a frontend engineer.

rounds.name: Agentic coding option
rounds.note: In October 2026 one senior candidate could choose a JavaScript interview or an agentic coding interview.

rounds.name: Final interviews
rounds.note: 4 to 6 hours with 4 to 6 people over 1 to 2 days, per the guide.

rounds.name: Decision
rounds.note: Within a week of the final interviews; the recruiter may ask for references at this stage.

rounds.name: Recruiter or HR screen
rounds.note: A call on your background, salary and the next steps; some recruiters add a short check of JavaScript or React theory.

rounds.name: HackerRank assessment
rounds.note: Three algorithm tasks in 85–110 minutes, done at home before a deadline; sometimes before the recruiter call.

rounds.name: Live coding
rounds.note: About an hour of TypeScript and React with an interviewer, from a prepared boilerplate or in CodeSandbox.

rounds.name: System design
rounds.note: A design round on a whiteboard, Excalidraw in a 2024 loop; a 2023 recruiter said it decides between mid and senior.

rounds.name: Team fit
rounds.note: A behavioural conversation about past experience.

rounds.name: Bar Raiser
rounds.note: An interview on how you work and make decisions; listed in recent plans, and no frontend review describes sitting it.

rounds.name: Screening call
rounds.note: A short call with a recruiter or HR on your background, your projects and what you want next.

rounds.name: JavaScript fundamentals
rounds.note: JavaScript questions and one to three coding problems, an hour long in a 2023 account.

rounds.name: Second technical round
rounds.note: A harder JavaScript round or an hour of algorithm problems, three of them in a 2023 account.

rounds.name: Design or machine coding
rounds.note: A small web app to design and build in plain JavaScript, or a coding problem and a UI to build.

rounds.name: Hiring manager
rounds.note: The hiring manager's round: JavaScript questions, a coding or design task, behavioural questions, or a mix of them.

variants.title: Front-end engineers, Ho Chi Minh City, 2025
variants.from: one account of a Ho Chi Minh City loop
variants.ask: Interviewing in Ho Chi Minh City?

rounds.name: HR call
rounds.note: Ho Chi Minh City loop, from one account: personal details, expected salary and whether you would move to Saigon.

rounds.name: Frontend technical round
rounds.note: About two hours in clear parts: CSS, JavaScript, a React build and an algorithm.

rounds.name: CS-fundamentals round
rounds.note: A design discussion that starts from your current work, then networking and security fundamentals.

rounds.name: Behavioural interview
rounds.note: After a pass notice a week later: how the candidate works, handles problems and communicates, and past difficulties.

rounds.name: Final conversation and offer
rounds.note: A light last round on future direction and expectations at Shopee, compared with the previous job.

variants.title: Fresh graduates, Singapore, 2020 to 2022
variants.ask: Interviewing as a fresh graduate in Singapore?

rounds.name: Online assessment
rounds.note: A 70-minute test in the 2022 account: multiple-choice on systems and networking plus two coding problems.

rounds.name: Technical rounds on a shared editor
rounds.note: One to three rounds of 60 to 90 minutes on a shared editor: coding problems, CS fundamentals and a design concept.

rounds.name: HR call with a verbal offer
rounds.note: A verbal offer from HR about five weeks after applying in the 2020 account; a 2022 loop ended in a rejection.

variants.title: Campus and social hires, mainland China, in Chinese, 2019 to 2022

rounds.name: Application or referral, then a written test
rounds.note: The campus posting lists an online application or referral, then a written test that some roles skip.

rounds.name: First technical interview
rounds.note: JavaScript, CSS, HTTP and framework basics plus one to three short coding tasks.

rounds.name: Second technical interview
rounds.note: Deeper framework, tooling and performance questions, scenarios, project depth and often a second coding task.

rounds.name: HR interview and offer
rounds.note: The posting lists an HR conversation before the offer.

variants.title: Front-end and software engineers, Taipei, 2021 to 2023

rounds.name: HR phone screen
rounds.note: A 30-minute HR call on background and the job in the 2021 account; the 2023 account lists an HR conversation first.

rounds.name: Onsite written test
rounds.note: A 90-minute written test on site: seven questions on JavaScript, CSS and React, rated junior level by the candidate.

rounds.name: Team interviews
rounds.note: Panels with a product manager and a tech lead on practical work, or a manager round and a peer round.

rounds.name: Senior-manager conversation
rounds.note: A last round with a senior manager, mostly a chat, in the 2023 account.

rounds.name: Recruiter call
rounds.note: A video or phone call with a recruiter, 5 to 30 minutes in the accounts, on your background and why Spotify.

rounds.name: Technical screen
rounds.note: 60 to 90 minutes with one or two engineers: JavaScript and CSS questions and a coding task.

rounds.name: Final: web practical
rounds.note: An hour in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript: a small feature or app to build, or web domain questions.

rounds.name: Final: algorithms
rounds.note: An hour on one or two coding problems, very basic to LeetCode medium in most accounts and hard in one 2025 loop.

rounds.name: Final: system design
rounds.note: An hour designing a product end to end, backend included.

rounds.name: Final: values
rounds.note: Values and behavioural questions, an hour with the hiring manager in a 2022 account and 30 minutes in a 2021 one.

rounds.name: Recruiter screen
rounds.note: About 30 minutes with a recruiter, by phone in the 2025 accounts, on your experience, your motivation and the role.

rounds.name: Technical screen
rounds.note: 60 minutes of live, multi-part coding in CoderPad, sometimes building a UI component.

rounds.name: Onsite: bug squash
rounds.note: Fix a bug in a codebase you have not seen: reproduce it, find the cause and get the existing tests passing.

rounds.name: Onsite: integration
rounds.note: Build a working piece of a feature with tools or an API you are given, reading their documentation as you go.

rounds.name: Onsite: programming exercise
rounds.note: A coding exercise with an engineer.

rounds.name: Onsite: frontend design
rounds.note: A design discussion, talked through rather than coded, about how you would structure a piece of frontend.

rounds.name: Onsite: manager conversation
rounds.note: A conversation with the hiring manager about your past work, how you work and your goals.

rounds.name: Recruiter or HR call
rounds.note: A recruiter or HR call came first in two accounts; in a third, a short introductory call followed the assessment.

rounds.name: Online assessment
rounds.note: Often on Codility: one account lists 2 hours for 5 questions, another a three-hour assessment.

rounds.name: Technical screen
rounds.note: A one-hour phone or video interview, or a live React coding session.

rounds.name: Final loop: frontend coding
rounds.note: One or two frontend coding rounds in React, or an Angular round followed by a TypeScript and JavaScript round.

rounds.name: Final loop: data structures and algorithms
rounds.note: One LeetCode-style algorithm round, which a 2020 recruiter planned as one of three coding rounds.

rounds.name: Final loop: frontend system design
rounds.note: One frontend system design round in the 2020 and 2024 onsite accounts.

rounds.name: Final loop: hiring manager and behavioural
rounds.note: A behavioural round; one recruiter's plan listed a hiring-manager and a product manager interview.

rounds.name: Team match
rounds.note: One 2026 account passed four technical rounds but got no offer because the team wanted a full-stack engineer.

rounds.name: Recruiter call
rounds.note: A phone call with a recruiter, in one account.

rounds.name: Technical rounds
rounds.note: One or two rounds that vary by team, mixing React coding, algorithms and UI component design.

rounds.name: System design final
rounds.note: A final-round system design interview, in one account.

rounds.name: Recruiter call
rounds.note: Virtual and 30 minutes with a recruiter or sourcer in the official guide.

rounds.name: Online assessment
rounds.note: HackerRank in the official guide; a 35-minute CodeSignal test in a 2022 account.

rounds.name: DSA round

rounds.name: Hiring manager

rounds.name: HR call

variants.title: SDE-2 and frontend engineer roles in India
variants.from: SDE-2 and frontend engineer roles in India
variants.ask: Interviewing for an SDE-2 role in India?

rounds.name: Online assessment
rounds.note: One 2024 assessment: multiple-choice on HTML, CSS, JavaScript and React or Angular, plus two easy coding questions.

rounds.name: Technical rounds
rounds.note: Two technical rounds of about an hour: data structures or a medium LeetCode problem, then React questions.

rounds.name: Final round
rounds.note: Questions on OOP, DBMS and past experience, with Java and React in one account.

variants.title: Software Engineer III, senior and frontend engineer roles
variants.from: Software Engineer III and senior roles
variants.ask: Interviewing for Software Engineer III or a senior role?

rounds.name: Online assessment (2026 accounts)
rounds.note: A HackerRank assessment with a coding problem and a React or Angular debugging task.

rounds.name: Coding screen
rounds.note: A Karat screen, a one-hour HackerRank interview, two React code challenges or a JavaScript coding round.

rounds.name: Coding rounds
rounds.note: One or two coding rounds: React coding, a debugging session, medium DSA problems or a UI and JavaScript round.

rounds.name: System design
rounds.note: One or two design rounds: high-level system design, or design questions about past projects.

rounds.name: Behavioural and hiring manager
rounds.note: A behavioural, team-fit or managerial round.

rounds.name: Sourcer or recruiter conversation
rounds.note: An initial conversation with a sourcer or recruiter, per the hiring page.

rounds.name: Phone or video interviews
rounds.note: One or two behavioural or technical interviews with a potential peer or manager, per the hiring page.

rounds.name: Virtual onsite
rounds.note: Up to five interviewers, potential teammates and cross-functional partners, about 45 minutes each, per the hiring page.

variants.title: Software engineers with a UI round, 2026
variants.from: a software engineer loop with a UI round
variants.ask: Interviewing as a software engineer with a UI round?

rounds.name: Recruiter screen
rounds.note: A recruiter call on the current role and backend experience, interest in Waymo and the shape of the process.

rounds.name: Progressive coding round
rounds.note: One problem whose constraints kept changing, judged on correctness and complexity.

rounds.name: JavaScript and UI round
rounds.note: A UI component built in plain JavaScript with no framework, followed by questions on the choices behind it.

rounds.name: Hiring-manager round
rounds.note: Conversational and scenario-based: production ownership, reliability and cross-team collaboration.

rounds.name: Algorithms round
rounds.note: A data structures and algorithms round closed the loop.

rounds.note: Technical team members, not recruiters, review the CV and a "statement of exceptional work".

rounds.name: Screening
rounds.note: A 15-minute "phone interview" with "some basic technical questions".

rounds.name: React coding interview
rounds.note: A small React app in TypeScript on Google Meet: 45 minutes in London, one or two interviews on Bay Area teams.

rounds.name: HTML/CSS interview
rounds.note: Implement a UI from a screenshot; 45 minutes with Tailwind in London. Postings only.

rounds.name: Coding assessment in a language of your choice
rounds.note: A general coding round before the frontend interviews. Postings only.

rounds.name: Systems hands-on
rounds.note: A live problem-solving session on practical skills. Posting only.

rounds.name: Meet the team or founding engineer
rounds.note: Bay Area: present your past work to a small audience. London: 30 minutes with a founding engineer.

rounds.name: UI design exercise and presentation
rounds.note: A UI design in a tool of your choice and a 20-minute presentation of past design work. Posting only.

rounds.name: Take-home and code-reading final
rounds.note: A four-hour take-home with AI coding assistants allowed, then a one-hour in-person coding round on existing code.

rounds.name: Talent acquisition call
rounds.note: 30 minutes with a talent acquisition partner on motivation, expectations and salary.
